article.title: Redis 8.10 Ships Compact Hashes, a Bulk-Insert HIMPORT Command, and Native BACKUP
article.summary: Redis 8.10 reaches general availability with a memory-saving compact hash encoding, a bulk-insert HIMPORT command, and a node-side BACKUP command built on multi-part AOF.
article.body_markdown:
## Overview

Redis 8.10 reached general availability on July 29, 2026, according to the release's [GitHub page](https://github.com/redis/redis/releases/tag/8.10.0), which describes it as "the General Availability release of Redis 8.10 in Redis Open Source." The release's headline addition is compact hashes, a new hash encoding paired with a bulk-loading command, alongside a native backup command and a batch of new list, set, and time-series commands, as detailed on Redis's [official "What's new" documentation page](https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/whats-new/8-10/).

## What We Know

- **Compact hashes cut memory use for uniform-schema keys.** According to the [release notes](https://github.com/redis/redis/releases/tag/8.10.0), compact hashes are "a new hash encoding that reduces memory usage by storing hash field names just once for keys that share a schema." The [documentation page](https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/whats-new/8-10/) adds that the feature ships with new configuration parameters — `hash-rdb-load-min-template-entries`, `hash-rdb-load-max-template-entries`, and `hash-rdb-load-template-disassembly-threshold` — and new metrics, including `INFO STATS` fields `hash_templates` and `hash_template_keys` and an `INFO MEMORY` field called `used_memory_hash_templates`.
- **A new `HIMPORT` command loads compact hashes in bulk.** The release notes describe `HIMPORT` as providing "high-throughput bulk insertion of compact hashes," according to [Redis's documentation](https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/whats-new/8-10/).
- **`BACKUP` adds node-side backup and restore.** The new `BACKUP` command is a "node-side implementation for backup and restore based on multi-part AOF (MP-AOF)," per the [release notes](https://github.com/redis/redis/releases/tag/8.10.0).
- **New list and set commands avoid materializing intermediate results.** `LMOVEM` and `BLMOVEM` "move multiple elements between lists in a single operation," while `SUNIONCARD` and `SDIFFCARD` return the cardinality of a set union or difference "without materializing the result," according to the [documentation](https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/whats-new/8-10/).
- **Stream reads can now be capped.** `XREAD` and `XREADGROUP` accept new `MAXCOUNT` and `MAXSIZE` arguments "to cap the cumulative number of reply entries and the cumulative reply size," the documentation states.
- **Search gains a stricter timeout mode and two new languages.** `FT.SEARCH`, `FT.AGGREGATE`, and `FT.HYBRID` "now enforce the query TIMEOUT more strictly," and the `search-on-timeout` policy gains a new `RETURN_STRICT` option that "return[s] best-effort partial results while enforcing the timeout through the post-processing (result) pipeline," according to the [documentation](https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/whats-new/8-10/). Separately, Redis Search adds stemmer support for Malay and Tagalog.
- **Time series gets new range and label-query commands.** `TS.NRANGE` and `TS.NREVRANGE` query across multiple time series and group results by timestamp, `TS.READ` performs an "optionally blocking read," and `TS.QUERYLABELS` returns a list of labels and label-values, according to both the [release notes](https://github.com/redis/redis/releases/tag/8.10.0) and the [documentation page](https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/whats-new/8-10/).
- **The release also closes a security issue.** Under a dedicated "Security fixes" heading, the documentation states that 8.10 "[f]ixed an issue where a user could manipulate data read by a connection by injecting `\r\n` sequences into a Redis error reply."
- **Redis 8.10 ships under Redis Open Source's tri-license model.** The project's [license file](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/redis/redis/8.10.0/LICENSE.txt) states that "[s]tarting with Redis 8, Redis Open Source is moving to a tri-licensing model," offering the Redis Source Available License 2.0, the Server Side Public License v1, or the GNU Affero General Public License v3 (AGPLv3) — the option that keeps Redis 8 available under an OSI-recognized open-source license.
- **The release is tested across a broad operating-system matrix.** Per the [release notes](https://github.com/redis/redis/releases/tag/8.10.0), Redis 8.10 is tested on Ubuntu 22.04, 24.04, and 26.04; Rocky Linux and AlmaLinux 8.10, 9.7, and 10.1; Debian 12.13 and 13.4; Alpine 3.23; and macOS Sonoma, Sequoia, and Tahoe on both Intel and ARM.

## What We Don't Know

Neither the release notes nor the documentation page quantifies how much memory compact hashes save in practice — the description is limited to the mechanism (storing shared field names once per schema) rather than a benchmarked percentage. Redis has not published independent third-party performance testing of the new encoding or the `HIMPORT` bulk-load path at the time of this release.
